question.prompt: Let \(a\) be a positive number. Consider the set \(S\) of all points whose rectangular coordinates \((x,y)\) satisfy all of the following conditions: \[ \begin{aligned} &\text{(i) }\frac a2\le x\le2a\\ &\text{(ii) }\frac a2\le y\le2a\\ &\text{(iii) }x+y\ge a\\ &\text{(iv) }x+a\ge y\\ &\text{(v) }y+a\ge x. \end{aligned} \] The boundary of set \(S\) is a polygon with

solutions.explanation:
Conditions (i) and (ii) describe the square
\[
\frac a2\le x\le2a,\qquad \frac a2\le y\le2a.
\]
Every point in this square already satisfies \(x+y\ge a\), because both coordinates are at least \(a/2\). Thus condition (iii) adds no side; its equality occurs only at the lower-left corner.

Condition (iv) is \(y\le x+a\). Its boundary line meets the left and top sides of the square at
\[
\left(\frac a2,\frac{3a}2\right),\qquad (a,2a),
\]
so it cuts off the upper-left corner. Similarly, condition (v), \(x\le y+a\), cuts off the lower-right corner, meeting the bottom and right sides at
\[
\left(\frac{3a}2,\frac a2\right),\qquad (2a,a).
\]
These cuts do not overlap: a point cannot satisfy both \(y-x>a\) and \(x-y>a\). Each new diagonal segment also satisfies the other inequality, so both remain on the boundary.

Since \(a>0\), all four intersection points lie strictly inside their respective square sides. Consequently, each of the four original sides retains a nonzero segment, and the two cuts contribute two additional sides. The polygon therefore has \(4+2=6\) sides, choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
solutions.title: Cut two corners from the square
